term: norm on claims (scope, standard, acceptable, counterexample)
definition: `Norm` has a scope and a standard on claims. Relative to an acceptance predicate (established, absolutely true, opined, …) it holds when every acceptable claim in scope meets the standard; a counterexample is an acceptable claim in scope that fails it. Self-application means that the norm's own formulation is in its scope.
note: Analytical schema for retorsion arguments (#397), meant to be reused by Clifford (#376), verificationism (#363) and Hume's scopes. It fixes no particular norm, scope or acceptance predicate; each instance supplies and sources its own.
